sentences.text:
Author: N.Tukaramji
Bench: N.Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.Tukaramji
 I.A.Nos. 3 and 4 Of 2025
 In/And
 Criminal Petition No.5308 Of 2025
Common Order

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS, 2023') seeking quashment of the proceedings against the petitioner/accused in S.C.
POCSO No.669 of 2022 on the file of I-Fast Track Special Judge for Trial and Disposal of Rape and POCSO Act Cases, Ranga Reddy District at Rajendra Nagar.
2. The petitioner is sole accused in the S.C. POCSO No.669 of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(2) (n) IPC and Section 5 (1) r/w. 6 of POCSO Act 2012.

3. Heard Mr.T.C.K Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, representing the respondent No.1-State and Mr.MD.Himad Pasha,
learned counsel for the respondent No.2/de-facto complainant.
4.

Pending this petition, the parties have entered into the compromise and, accordingly, respondent No.2/de-facto complainant filed I.A.Nos.3 and 4 of 2025 with the prayer to permit them to enter into compromise 2 NTR,J I.A.Nos. 3 and 4 of 2025 in/and and by recording the settlement to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused in S.C. POCSO No.669 of 2022.
5. This Court vide order dated 18.06.2025 referred the parties to the High Court Legal Services Committee for identification and to verify the voluntariness in arriving the settlement.

The Secretary, High Court Legal Services Committee, has submitted report dated 25.06.2025 stating that the parties were identified by their respective counsel and also on verification of Aadhar Cards/Identity Cards and the enquiries revealed that the parties have willfully and without coercion entered into settlement/compromise.
6.
I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and perused the materials on record.

7. Having considered the allegations, the nature of charged offences and taking into account the amicable settlement between the parties and to restore peace between the parties, in the light of the dictums in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and another 1 and Anil Mishra v. State of U.P. 2; State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and others 3, this Court is of the considered view that quashment of the impugned 2012 (10) SCC 303 2024 INSC 189 2019 (5) SCC 688 3 NTR,J I.A.Nos.
